sites.name: La Vallée blanche, Tahiti

s1.quote: The Vallée Blanche dive site, known as the most famous in Tahiti … Exposed to currents, this site … Vallée Blanche is possible at 20 meters , making it ideal for intermediate divers

s2.quote: The white valley is one of the top dive spots in Tahiti famous for its diverse marine life – especially sharks. … The current here is just right for it.

highlights.text: Several shark species incl. blacktip, lemon
Good drift dive along a white-sand strip

summary.text: Tahiti's best-known shark dive, just off the airport reef on the northwest coast. Currents carry divers past grey, blacktip, whitetip and lemon sharks, plus jacks and barracuda, over a pale sand channel. A drift dive best suited to divers with some experience.

sites.depthNote: Around 20 m typical; deeper (40 m) for experienced divers

s1.quote: Suitable for all levels, The Source offers exceptional biodiversity … The coral reef extends from 0 to 10 meters and descends to 20 or 40 meters for experienced divers.

s2.quote: The Spring also called La Source is a popular dive site known for its turtles and the freshwater spring gushing out under the water. … there’s no such current to worry about, so it’s great for beginners too.

highlights.text: Green and hawksbill turtles
Freshwater spring emerging at about 8 m

summary.text: A gentle west-coast reef dive off Puna'auia, popular for turtle sightings and a freshwater spring bubbling up from the seabed. Shallow, current-free and clear, so it suits newer divers, with deeper sections for experienced ones.

sites.name: La Faille d Arue

s1.quote: The Arue Fault in northern Tahiti invites divers to glide along a stunning coral wall. The wall begins at about 15 feet below the surface … the ocean here is usually calm and the current is minimal. This makes this site great for beginners and intermediate divers.

highlights.text: Coral wall with a cave/fault at about 80 ft

sites.depthNote: Wall starts about 15 ft; most diving 50-80 ft, cave near 80 ft

s1.quote: Located in the lagoon of Faa’a , the Aquarium dive site is a natural reserve hosting a rich marine biodiversity. … spread across an area with a maximum depth of 13 meters .

s2.quote: Aquarium is the one to go for. It’s a wreck dive located on the west coast of Tahiti. This site is max 40 feet deep and usually has good visibility around 40-60 feet.

highlights.text: Cessna plane and two small boat wrecks

summary.text: A sheltered lagoon dive off Faa'a built around a small plane wreck and two boats. Shallow and nearly current-free, it is a go-to spot for training dives and first-timers, with lionfish and plenty of reef fish around the wrecks.

s1.quote: un hydravion Catalyna , dont la pénétration est possible … une goélette d’environ 40 mètres repose à une profondeur de 8 à 22 mètres.

penetration.value: The Catalina seaplane can be entered

highlights.text: Catalina seaplane wreck, schooner and a third boat

sites.name: Les 3 Pitons

s1.quote: Located near The Source , the 3 Pitons dive site features an impressive underwater landscape , where three pinnacles rise from 40 meters to stop at depths of 10 and 5 meters . Each pinnacle is accompanied by a freshwater spring

highlights.text: Three pinnacles each with a freshwater spring
Turtles, surgeonfish, clownfish

sites.depthNote: Pinnacles rise from 40 m to tops at 10 m and 5 m

s1.quote: le Tombant Saint-Étienne offre un superbe tombant où il est possible de croiser des tortues , des bancs de perches pagaie

s2.quote: St. Etienne Drop-Off … It’s actually a wall dive with vertical reef walls dropping down about 200 feet (60 meters). … There’s usually gentle current which allows drift diving. … better suited for divers with some experience.

highlights.text: Turtles and paddle perch along the wall

summary.text: A steep reef wall just beyond the barrier reef on Tahiti's west coast, close to the Ta'apuna pass. Turtles and schools of reef fish cruise the upper wall, and gentle current often allows a drift. Better with some experience; wind can make it hard to dive.

s1.quote: The Zélée was a French gunboat of the Surprise-class … Today, the wreck rests near Papeete , at a depth of 5 to 20 meters . … Accessible to divers of all levels

highlights.text: Coral-covered WWI gunboat wreck scuttled 1914

s1.quote: Papa Whiskey dive site gets its name from its proximity to the Papeete West (PW) aviation beacon … Shaped like an amphitheater … a steep drop-off at 50 meters and stunning sea fans at 40 meters

s2.quote: Papa Whisky is one of the amazing dive sites for pelagic observations. … It reaches max depths around 160 feet. At about 65 feet, you’ll find plenty of lively reefs and fish.

highlights.text: Whitetip, blacktip and grey reef sharks
Sea fans at 40 m

summary.text: An amphitheatre-shaped reef on the west coast away from any pass, known for pelagic sightings. Reef sharks and turtles patrol a small drop-off, with lively coral from around 20 m and a steeper wall deeper down for advanced divers.

sites.name: Le piton aux gorgones

s1.quote: le Piton aux Gorgones est un site spectaculaire réservé aux plongeurs expérimentés. Ce sec vertigineux, couvert de magnifiques gorgones , remonte des abysses jusqu’à -42 mètres.

highlights.text: Gorgonian-covered pinnacle, whitetip sharks, turtles

sites.depthNote: Pinnacle rises from deep water to about 42 m (per operator)

s1.quote: La passe du gouverneur (ou fausse passe de Paea PK18) est une plongée très originale avec un départ dans le lagon pour profiter d’un vol de raie léopard. Puis dérivante jusque dans l’océan. … Profondeur : de 5m à 35m

s2.quote: La Fausse Passe de Paea Pronfondeur : de 12m à 32m

highlights.text: Leopard rays, turtles, whitetip sharks

s1.quote: The maximum depth the Canyons reaches is about 90 feet … occasional strong currents … a great dive spot for divers of all levels.

s2.quote: The Canyons Depth, duration, and visibility Typical max depth : 14–27 meters (45–90 feet) … Visibility : Usually 20–30 meters (65–100 feet)

highlights.text: Blacktip sharks, green turtles, anemones

summary.text: A reef dive on Moorea's north side near Opunohu Bay, where coral canyons shelter small fish and blacktip sharks cruise past. Mostly calm and open to all levels, but currents can pick up and catch newer divers out.

s1.quote: Eden Park is an amazing dive site that goes down to 70 feet, and offers diving opportunities for divers of all levels.

s2.quote: Eden Park Depth, duration, and visibility Typical dive depth : 15–21 meters (50–70 feet) … Visibility : Clear waters with visibility typically 20–30 meters (65–100 feet)

highlights.text: Blacktip sharks, rare lemon shark, turtles

summary.text: A relaxed reef dive just beyond the lagoon off Moorea's north coast, next to the Canyons. Healthy coral and anemones attract turtles, barracuda and blacktip sharks, with the odd shy lemon shark. Suitable for most certified divers.

s1.quote: True to its name, the Coral Wall site is packed with tons of coral reefs forming walls and beautiful canyons on the seafloor. It has a maximum depth of 90 feet (27 meters)

s2.quote: Coral Wall Depth, duration, and visibility Typical max depth : 14–27 meters (45–90 feet)

highlights.text: Blacktip reef sharks and turtles along coral walls

summary.text: A sheltered coral-wall dive near Opunohu Bay, split into three sections so it can fill several tanks. Calm water and shallow-to-moderate depths make it comfortable for beginners, with reef sharks, turtles and morays along the walls.

s1.quote: Taotoi is a well-liked Moorea dive site where you can witness vast sea life in a single area. The site isn’t too deep, only around 50 feet which is perfect for beginners. There can be light to moderate currents

s2.quote: Taotoi Depth, duration, and visibility Typical max depth : 15 meters (50 feet)

highlights.text: Blacktip sharks, eagle rays, turtles, giant morays

summary.text: A shallow outer-lagoon dive on Moorea's north shore, close to the Taotoi channel where fish stream between lagoon and ocean. Easy depths suit beginners, with blacktip sharks, eagle rays, turtles and large moray eels.

s1.quote: The Mamaru dive site is another popular choice on Moorea, a great dive for beginner divers … But the real stars of the show are the reef sharks: both blacktop reef sharks (more common) and whitetip (less common).

highlights.text: Blacktip and whitetip reef sharks, turtles

s1.quote: Tiputa Pass is one of French Polynesia's most dynamic drift dives … Difficulty Advanced Depth 12–40 m Visibility 30 m

s2.quote: Tiputa Pass (Incoming Current) The Sharks’ cavern : This dive is best done by experienced divers.

highlights.text: Grey reef sharks, jacks, barracuda, rays

hazards.text: Strong tidal current; drift technique needed

s1.quote: Motu Nuhi-Nuhi (aquarium) Lagoon The Motu Nuhi Nuhi is a little coral islet located in the lagoon along the axis of the Tiputa pass … This site, shallow and sheltered from currents, is ideal for novice divers

highlights.text: Coral garden with many colourful fish
